extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors and writers preparing to pitch to literary agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and delivering a tight, well-rehearsed 30-second (elevator) pitch to literary agents to elicit interest and a next step. Focuses on what to say, how to present credentials, and how to close with a call to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity / 30-second time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to pitch your idea in 30 seconds or fewer (an “Elevator Pitch”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft just a few key sentences and commit them to memory. The page emphasizes a 'tight, well-rehearsed pitch' so you never waste an opportunity; practice delivery and keep it short so you can deliver it in person between other duties the agent has.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the literary agent who you are
rubrics_metrics.description: State your name and job title, or the title of the position you're seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example phrasing from the page: “Hi, my name is Miranda Mechanic, and I’m a licensed automotive mechanic who writes how-to articles for women who don’t want their cars to get the best of them.” Keep this line concise and informative so the agent immediately knows who you are and your relevant professional identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State what you want (clear objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't beat around the bush — explicitly state what you're after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “I’m interested in placing some of my articles with your magazine, Auto Care for Everybody.” Make your objective direct (e.g., representation, article placement, book deal) so the agent knows what action to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show why you're the best choice (relevant credentials)
rubrics_metrics.description: List degrees, writing credentials, training or experience that relate to what you're seeking; if you lack direct experience, name relevant qualities or skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice includes matching qualifications to the stated goal (don’t list unrelated credentials). Anti-pattern: “Saying you want to write an article on mechanics and then listing your degrees in early Russian literature won’t help.” If no formal credentials, cite traits like attention to detail or passion. Be brief and memorable — find the 'special something' that separates you from the crowd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a call to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Finish by asking for what you want or proposing the next step to prompt further interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example call to action: “I’d like to show you copies of my articles, including ‘How to Change a Tire When It’s Twenty Below Zero’ and ‘How to Add Oil When You’re Wearing a Power Suit.’ ” The page stresses that the call to action 'is what leads to further interaction' and warns not to neglect this step; take a deep breath and ask directly.
